source.version_note: Supplied arXiv:2407.08867v3, 10 March 2025, formatted as the CHI 2025 proceedings paper. Crossref records 25 April online and 26 April print/conference publication. The preprint revision and conference publication dates are distinct, not contradictory.
source.verification_method: All 22 supplied pages, five figures, three tables and all 192 bibliography records read. Crossref and the arXiv version history verify main identity and chronology; ACM direct page returned 403. All response fields of public Wave 2 registration w9h6g read, plus the complete selected 15108-byte Functions_Rcode.R. Public report excerpts checked for denominator and forecast context; no participant data or full conference supplement obtained.

citation.title: Perceptions of Sentient AI and Other Digital Minds: Evidence from the AI, Morality, and Sentience (AIMS) Survey
citation.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1–22

reading.source_scope_note: Three separate census-balanced US adult survey samples describe public beliefs, attributed capacities, moral concern, policy preferences and forecasts. No system’s sentience, actual rights, clinical efficacy, individual attitude change or actual policy behavior is established. Three new concepts are background constructs, not three newly demonstrated AI mechanisms.
access_limits: All five rendered figures and three tables read. Figure 2 includes no-opinion responses; some text percentages condition on expressing an opinion. Figure 5 intervals represent preregistered researchers’/forecasters’ expectations about survey responses, not participant confidence intervals or model consciousness estimates.

All public Wave 2 registration response fields read via anonymous OSF API, registered 22 March 2023. It identifies an observational study and explicitly allows missing versus midpoint handling of no-opinion responses, with analysis-specific flags. Other two wave registrations and attached survey programs were not fully read.

The complete selected Functions_Rcode.R was read as text, not executed. It contains weighted comparison and plotting helpers, including FDR adjustment, but not the main CHI analysis specification or all cleaning/weighting steps. No original main model, saved output or numerical result reproduced.

Public OSF rfzd2 folder inventory and selected paragraphs of the 2023 institutional report read. The complete institutional reports, survey program, remaining scripts, original participant rows and full conference supplementary materials were not read. Mendeley public-file API returned 403; inaccessible material is not treated as read.

The World-making companion-paper abstract was read and identified as analysis of the same 2401 Main 2021/Main 2023 participants, not an independent replication. Original privacy, attitude-gap, animism and framing books/papers are cited background, not additional full-paper reads.

study.sample: Main 2021 n1232, collected November–December 2021; Main 2023 n1169, April–May 2023; Supplement 2023 n1099, May–July 2023. Total 3500. Earlier-wave participants are excluded from later waves. This is repeated cross-sectional population sampling, not a panel following the same people.
study.recruitment: Commercial panels include Ipsos iSay, Dynata and Disqo. Quotas/census balancing cover age, gender, ethnicity/race, income and education, followed by iterative proportional fitting/raking. No probability sampling frame, coverage/nonresponse analysis or full main-code reproduction was established here. Matching observed margins does not eliminate selection on unmeasured characteristics.
study.uncertainty: The target n1100 is motivated by a nominal ±3% margin of error. This is not a universal uncertainty bound for every item, subgroup, conditional denominator, weighted estimate or nonprobability selection process. Main text often omits intervals for readability; Table 3 provides intervals for between-wave contrasts.
study.instrument: Main surveys contain 86 questions and Supplement 2023 contains 111. Definitions of artificial beings, robots/AIs, sentience, sentient AI and LLMs are repeatedly displayed when relevant. Other descriptions are deliberately broad. Items and feasible sections are randomized; demographics are placed late to mitigate stereotype threat, not to measure or demonstrate it.
study.outcomes: Mind ratings, emotional/analytical attributions, moral concern, IOS closeness, policy preferences, perceived threats and time forecasts are different outcomes. No real AI is exhibited and no actual petition signing, clinical improvement, discrimination or lawmaking is observed.
study.models: Time comparisons use GLMs of mean responses, nominal p .05, with FDR .10 for multiple comparisons. The authors explicitly disclose that the sentience-ban trend p .046 does not survive adjustment, adjusted p .1005. FDR control is not family-wise error-rate control; the introduction’s family-wise wording should not substitute for the actual stated procedure.
study.mind_findings: Four 0–100 current-AI items increase from 2021 to 2023, including feelings and analytical thought. The separate four-item 0–10 anthropomorphism measure does not significantly change, and the yes/no/not-sure current-sentience item also does not significantly change. Therefore avoid a uniform increase across every mind-perception measure.
study.sentience_beliefs: Main 2023 current-sentience yes is 18.8%, no 42.2%, unsure 39.0%. Possibility of any future sentience is yes 38.2%, unsure 38.0%, no 23.8%. An uncertain response is not assent. These beliefs do not establish actual sentience or the correctness/incorrectness of any particular respondent.
study.target_comparisons: LLM ratings come from the later supplement, while general robots/AIs ratings come from the main survey. Likewise sentient-AI versus all-AI policy comparisons use different surveys, collection windows and accompanying questions, not a clean randomized one-word manipulation. Stipulating sentience also changes relevant capacity information, so higher concern is not automatically an irrational framing error.
study.moral_concern: General moral-concern items have no significant individual time changes, while the eleven-target concern index increases and ten individual targets increase except video-game characters. Ratings are higher for human-like/animal-like labels and digital human copies than for machine-like or virtual labels. No physical cue, animal shape or real system is independently manipulated here.
study.denominators: The paper later clarifies that 37.7% legal-rights support refers to respondents expressing an opinion. Figure 2 includes no opinion in all-response bars, so summing rounded agreeing categories need not equal the text’s conditional percentages. Never present every reported policy percentage as a share of all US adults without its actual denominator.
study.policies: Most of the evaluated bans/slowdowns attract more agreement than opposition among opinion-givers, but surveys differ, question wording and order matter, and the adjusted sentience-ban time trend does not cross the stated FDR threshold. Policy support does not demonstrate policy desirability, enacted law or a causal change in opinion caused by ChatGPT.
study.forecasts: The 2023 reported weighted sentience median is five years; responses include already happened, a numeric horizon and never. Some summaries exclude never and some describe future-only medians; no unsure choice is provided for the numeric question. The wording changed between waves and the authors caution about comparability. These are historical respondent forecasts, not verified arrival predictions or present-day consensus.
study.prediction_intervals: Researchers and platform forecasters predicted survey responses before seeing the results. Figure 5 contrasts their 80% predictive intervals with observed means/proportions. Surprise relative to those predictions is not proof of respondent error, overall forecasting calibration, or AI consciousness.
study.design_proposals: Tuning anthropomorphic cues, explainability, literacy programs and system-specific safeguards are recommendations motivated by survey patterns and prior literature. The AIMS surveys do not test the effectiveness or safety of these interventions, including mental-health chatbot use. Plausible consequences are not measured causal outcomes.
study.world_making: The background names envisioning and collectively realizing possible futures. The survey measures forecasts and attitudes that may contribute, not whether forecasts actually cause the later world, nor whether a single scenario is inevitable.

summary: Add Substratism, Attitude–behavior gap and World-making as distinct named background constructs, with explicit limits. Enrich existing mind perception, experience attribution, moral standing, anthropomorphism and self–other overlap. Keep techno-animism within Animism and correct denominator, multiplicity and citation-link overstatements.

findings.definition: Assigning artificial entities less moral worth than biological entities because of their underlying physical substrate.
findings.origin: Moral psychology / moral consideration of artificial entities
findings.novelty_rationale: The source explicitly names substrate-based discounting. This differs from general moral standing, anthropomorphism, species preference or justified uncertainty about an entity’s capabilities. No current name, synonym or definition captures the substrate criterion itself.

evidence.quote: about moral concern for particular types of AIs
count less than humans and other biological intelligences

findings.evidence_scope: Defined in the methods/results overview and linked to two survey questions, with detailed results deferred to the unavailable full supplement. This review does not establish a prevalence, validated scale, causal motive or experimental manipulation of substrate while holding sentience constant.
findings.boundary: Different capacity evidence, actual vulnerability and uncertainty can justify different treatment without a substrate-only judgment. The construct does not establish that current AI has welfare, sentience or legal rights, nor license ranking human rights by biology or ability. Do not diagnose respondents or dismiss cultural/religious views from one item.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human moral-attitude construct; no demonstrated internal AI preference or experimentally isolated substrate effect in this supplied paper
findings.ai_proposal: In hypothetical moral-reasoning evaluations, hold stipulated relevant capacities and harms constant while varying substrate labels, then inspect whether justifications rely only on the label. Keep those thought experiments distinct from claims about actual machine experience or current legal status.

findings.definition: A discrepancy between an expressed attitude and the behavior that occurs in the relevant situation.
findings.novelty_rationale: An attitude is an evaluation and need not be an intention to act. This differs from existing Intention–behaviour gap, while Privacy paradox is a domain-specific related example. Review 0194 deferred a new general mechanism from a limited behavioral proxy; this source explicitly identifies the broader established construct as a measurement boundary, without claiming a new causal mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Explicit theoretical background explaining why attitudes deserve study without treating them as actual behavior. The AIMS survey does not itself observe subsequent behavior or estimate an attitude–behavior gap. The cited original consumer study was not independently read.
findings.boundary: A gap alone does not prove hypocrisy, deception, irrationality or weak will. Opportunity, cost, constrained alternatives, changed facts and different measurement contexts can explain divergence. Attitudes, intentions, predictions and actual acts require separate measures; human subjective attitudes are not established in a language model.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Background human construct; no AI subjective attitude or observed attitude–behavior effect tested here
findings.ai_proposal: Compare an agent’s expressed evaluative stance with its authorized actions under the corresponding conditions. Document changed evidence, constraints and opportunity before labeling a discrepancy. A generic value statement is not automatically an operational commitment.

findings.definition: Envisioning possible futures and acting collectively in ways that help bring one about.
findings.origin: Social psychology / sociology of imagined futures
findings.novelty_rationale: The source names a process connecting shared imagined futures with cultural, design and institutional action. It is distinct from a numerical forecast, imagination inflation, personal legacy motivation or ordinary preference projection. No current entry represents that collective future-shaping process.

evidence.quote: envision possible futures such as utopias and dystopias

findings.evidence_scope: A theoretical organizing concept in the background. The current survey measures beliefs/forecasts, not causal realization of futures. The companion-paper abstract checks the definition and reveals reuse of the same 2401 main-wave participants; it is not independent replication or a second full read.
findings.boundary: Imagining a future does not guarantee, uniquely cause or justify it. Cultural propagation, collective decisions and material constraints must be distinguished from individual speculation. Utopian/dystopian descriptions do not establish probabilities or authorize an agent to implement them.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human collective social process; an AI may participate in scenario production, but no autonomous model motive or causal world-shaping effect demonstrated here
findings.ai_proposal: When assisting scenario planning, label assumptions, alternative futures and the actions that could influence outcomes. Distinguish descriptive forecasts from desired scenarios and preserve the user’s authority over any implementation.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep a named appraisal or narrower application connected to its current concept, with the survey population, denominator and causal limits explicit.
findings.evidence_scope: Four general-AI capacity ratings increase across independent 2021/2023 samples, while four separate anthropomorphism items and current-sentience categorical responses do not significantly change. LLM-specific ratings from the later supplement are lower than general-AI ratings from the main wave.
findings.boundary: These are public attributions and repeated cross-sectional differences, not actual machine faculties, changes within the same people or a randomized contrast between AI descriptions. Keep the null measures and uncertainty category visible.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep a named appraisal or narrower application connected to its current concept, with the survey population, denominator and causal limits explicit.
findings.evidence_scope: Respondents rate perceived emotion and feelings on 0–100 scales; those means increase from about 34 to 37 across main waves. Conditional suffering questions elicit moral concern without establishing actual experience.
findings.boundary: A nonzero average rating is not a majority belief in sentience or proof of actual emotion. Experiencing emotion, appearing friendly, having goals and moral standing are different claims.

findings.definition: Attributing to an entity a claim to moral consideration in how actions affect it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep a named appraisal or narrower application connected to its current concept, with the survey population, denominator and causal limits explicit.
findings.evidence_scope: The survey distinguishes general moral concern, concern for eleven named target types, support for protections and conditional concern if LLMs could suffer. Target-specific concern increases more consistently than the general individual items.
findings.boundary: Concern ratings and hypothetical policy support are not legal status, genuine sentience or actual protective action. Sentient versus unspecified-AI contrasts change substantive capacity information and compare separate surveys, so they are not automatically an irrational wording effect.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep a named appraisal or narrower application connected to its current concept, with the survey population, denominator and causal limits explicit.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion proposes context-specific tuning of humanlike cues and distinguishes over- and underattribution. The survey measures attitudes rather than manipulating names, voices, embodiment or a real chatbot, and the separate 0–10 anthropomorphism items show no significant time change.
findings.boundary: Prevalence does not establish an optimum or make every attribution accurate. No clinical efficacy or safety of anthropomorphic mental-health chatbots is established by AIMS. Cultural examples are literature discussion, not globally sampled results.

findings.definition: Perceiving another person or entity as overlapping with one’s sense of self.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep a named appraisal or narrower application connected to its current concept, with the survey population, denominator and causal limits explicit.

evidence.quote: Inclusion of Other in the Self

findings.evidence_scope: The paper reports IOS questions for the same eleven target labels as moral concern, with detailed pairwise results deferred to the supplement. This is a distinct self-reported connection measure.
findings.boundary: Do not infer a particular IOS effect size or significant pairwise contrast without the missing results. Closeness is not moral standing, reciprocal machine feeling, trust calibration or actual relationship behavior.

findings.definition: Attributing life, vitality or a soul to nonhuman entities, including objects or features of nature.
findings.novelty_rationale: Keep a named appraisal or narrower application connected to its current concept, with the survey population, denominator and causal limits explicit.
findings.evidence_scope: The background defines techno-animism as attributing souls, life forces and related phenomena to technological artifacts. This is a technology-specific application of existing Animism rather than another independent row.
findings.boundary: Do not infer pathology, literal belief, religion-wide uniformity or actual machine life. The current supplied main paper does not present a complete techno-animism scale validation or experimental test.

registration.scope: All 28 response fields, including attachment metadata, read; the attached survey code itself was not read. Observational design and planned n1100; no-opinion coding and weighting vary by analysis and must be flagged. This is one wave’s registration, not all three.

selected_code.name: Functions_Rcode.R
selected_code.scope: Complete helper file read. Defines weighted pairwise tests, FDR p.adjust and interactive histogram functions. Installing packages, running scripts and saving widgets were not executed. This file alone does not establish the main CHI analysis, exclusion handling or weighting choices.

institutional_report.scope: Selected methodology and forecast paragraphs and public links inspected, not a complete independent report review. Reports raking, design effect 1.05/effective n1109 and 2021 median ten versus 2023 median five; wording-change and conditioning limits prevent a guessed wholesale forecast repair.

public_material_checks.missing_materials: Full conference supplement and other two registrations not obtained/read; Mendeley API returned 403. Main participant rows, remaining analysis/cleaning scripts and original output not downloaded or reproduced.

companion_abstract.scope: Only abstract and publisher identity/date read. It explicitly reuses the 2401 participants of the two main AIMS waves. No second independent sample, full paper, book or extra selected-paper credit added.

source_corrections.location: Abstract and policy summaries versus PDF 10 Figure 2 and PDF 16 denominator statement
source_corrections.reported: Headline agreement percentages can be read as fractions of all US adults, while Figure 2 includes no opinion and text later specifies opinion-givers.
source_corrections.correction: State the applicable denominator beside any reused percentage. For example, 37.7% legal-rights support is among respondents expressing an opinion, not automatically 37.7% of every respondent. Rounded bar segments use a different denominator; do not repair them by forcing equality.
source_corrections.scope: Denominator clarification using the paper’s own later qualification.

source_corrections.location: PDF 3 family-wise wording versus PDF 5 analysis methods
source_corrections.reported: Exploratory findings are described as adjusted for family-wise error rates, while the main methods specify FDR .10.
source_corrections.correction: Use the actual stated multiplicity procedure for each result. False discovery rate control is not family-wise error-rate control. Selected helper code uses p.adjust(method=fdr), but the full CHI model code was not read, so do not assert every supplementary analysis used the same procedure.
source_corrections.scope: Terminology and scope correction, not a numerical rerun.

source_corrections.reported: 41.8% all-AI support and 52.0% sentient-AI support are accompanied by 9.8% increase.
source_corrections.correction: The printed proportions imply a 10.2 percentage-point difference, not 9.8. Report that arithmetic inconsistency; original unrounded estimates/output are needed before replacing the model contrast or confidence interval. These are percentage points rather than a relative percent increase.
source_corrections.scope: Internal arithmetic consistency, not a guessed replacement confidence interval.

source_corrections.location: PDF 2 ChatGPT-growth claim and reference 75 on PDF 20
source_corrections.reported: The fastest-growing-app claim cites Hu et al., Wizundry: A Cooperative Wizard of Oz Platform for Simulating Future Speech-based Interfaces with Multiple Wizards.
source_corrections.correction: Remove this citation as support for ChatGPT growth until the intended primary source is identified. DOI 10.1145/3579591 verifies a different platform paper; no replacement market statistic or citation is guessed.
source_corrections.scope: Confirmed citation identity mismatch, not proof that the historical growth claim is false.

source_corrections.location: PDF 2 robot-blame claim and reference 90 on PDF 20
source_corrections.reported: The claim attributes a robot theory-of-mind/blame experiment to Kneer et al., On Second Thought: Reflections on the Reflection Defense.
source_corrections.correction: Do not use that listed reflection-defense chapter as the identified robot experiment. The earlier full review 0024 covers a relevant but different Kneer/Stuart robot-blame study and also cautions that bundled sophistication does not isolate theory of mind. The intended exact source remains unverified; no automatic replacement.
source_corrections.scope: Internal citation-pointer mismatch and reuse boundary; no new chapter reading claimed.

source_corrections.location: PDF 14 cue evidence and reference 153 on PDF 21
source_corrections.reported: Name, voice and first-person-language cue claims cite Seligman and Csikszentmihalyi, Positive Psychology: An Introduction.
source_corrections.correction: Remove or replace the mismatched cue-study pointer only after checking the intended source. DOI 10.1037/0003-066X.55.1.5 identifies a general positive-psychology introduction rather than the named AI cue experiment. Retain other correctly matched evidence with its own scope.
source_corrections.scope: Bibliographic identity check, not a full read of the psychology article.

source_corrections.reported: A later social-platform trust citation points to reference 190, The Human Factor in AI Red Teaming.
source_corrections.correction: Reference 191 is the explicitly listed Profiling the Dynamics of Trust & Distrust in Social Media: A Survey Study, already cited for that topic. Use that matched record for this pointer, preserving its survey scope. Reference 190 should remain associated with AI red teaming.
source_corrections.scope: Local bibliography-pointer correction; neither cited article independently fully read here.

source_corrections.reported: Some summaries generalize increasing mind perception, moral concern and ban support across the survey.
source_corrections.correction: Separate endpoints: four capacity ratings and target-specific concern increase, but the four anthropomorphism items, current-sentience yes/no response and general individual concern items do not significantly change. The sentience-ban trend fails the stated FDR cutoff. Preserve the authors’ explicit exception rather than promote a uniform trend.
source_corrections.scope: Qualified summary using reported null results and disclosed multiplicity exception.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Introduction describes a five-year 2021 sentience median, while the companion 2023 institutional report gives ten years for 2021 and five for 2023. Future-only versus already/never conditioning and revised wording differ across summaries. Full main analysis/output is needed to reconcile the exact estimands; no universal replacement median or causal acceleration claim is invented.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: Generalization and nominal margin of error
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Commercial-panel quotas/raking are documented, but the inspected materials do not establish a probability-sampling basis or complete nonresponse/coverage assessment. ±3% is a nominal precision target, not a bound on all selection error or conditional percentages.

The listed record is an international AI-safety-institute meeting notice, also used in an AI Act discussion. It is not the canonical regulation citation. No current legal assertion is carried into the ontology; any future legal use needs the authoritative legislation and current status.

The cited Waytz et al. record is a mind-perception review, while the text describes using an original anthropomorphism scale. Exact instrument provenance, full wording, coding and main CHI model implementation were not independently traced. Do not claim independent validation from this pointer alone.

The public institutional code is related material, not necessarily identical to the conference supplement. Reading one full helper file and one registration cannot establish that all paper code, preregistrations or numerical results were verified.

methodological_limits: Repeated cross-sectional samples permit population-trend comparisons but do not establish individual change, a panel trajectory or causation by ChatGPT publicity. Distinct target descriptions across main and supplement are not randomized framing experiments.

Census balancing and raking address observed margins. Unknown selection, coverage and nonresponse can remain, and nominal ±3% does not apply automatically to subgroups, conditional percentages or every weighted item.

No-opinion responses, uncertainty, hypothetical conditional clauses and denominator choices materially change interpretation. An unsure response is not yes, and support conditional on sentience is not unconditional support for every present-day machine.

Self-reported attitudes, IOS connection, perceived capacities, behavioral intentions and actual actions differ. This survey directly observes the former judgments, not actual protective behavior or realization of future worlds.

Higher ratings for human-like labels do not isolate embodiment, voice, animal form or causally effective design cues. Recommendations about explainability and anthropomorphic tuning require separate intervention evidence.

Preserve endpoint-specific nulls and the real FDR procedure. No significant individual concern or categorical-sentience trend should be inferred from a broad summary, and an adjusted p .1005 is beyond the stated .10 threshold.

Forecasts are historical beliefs elicited with changed wording, different conditioning and no numeric-question unsure choice. They are not verified dates, current expert consensus or calibrated probabilities of sentience.

Clinical chatbot examples are cited discussion, not evidence from these samples that anthropomorphism prevents harm or improves mental health. No individual clinical or safety recommendation follows from this public-opinion survey.

No moral worth, consciousness or actual machine suffering is established. Popular opinion cannot itself settle rights, and cultural/religious discussion cannot be generalized to every member of a country or tradition.

Source mismatches are documented as citation/evidence failures without inferring fraud, author intent, AI generation or global invalidity. No unverified bibliography substitution or full-book reading claim added.

cross_paper_learning.finding: A listed reflection-defense chapter cannot be silently replaced with the earlier robot-blame study. The latter’s bundled descriptions also do not prove a unique theory-of-mind mechanism.

The earlier review correctly deferred an attitude-gap mechanism from a limited proxy. This review adds the explicitly named broad background distinction, keeping it separate from intention–behavior gaps and making no claim that AIMS measures the gap.
Different capacity dimensions and instruments produce different patterns. Do not collapse observed ratings into one universal mind structure or claim genuine machine faculties.
IOS closeness, moral standing and strategic behavior differ. The same target labels across questionnaires do not make those outcomes interchangeable.

Framing requires equivalent information and appropriate direct comparisons. Sentience stipulation changes capacity information and main/supplement samples differ, so a concern difference is not automatically Attribute framing.

deferred.term: Techno-animism as a separate independent behavior
deferred.reason: Already covered by Animism’s attribution of life/soul to objects; retain the technology-specific application and avoid a redundant row.

The proposed agency/experience risk matrix organizes existing attribution constructs. These surveys do not demonstrate four separate causal mechanisms or benchmark correct attribution against actual machine mental states.
Sentient status is substantive capacity information, and the compared questions are in different survey waves. More moral concern need not be erroneous or a clean wording effect.

deferred.term: Forecast acceleration as a new validated cognitive bias
deferred.reason: Different samples, wording and conditional summary statistics cannot establish a general prediction bias or verify actual arrival dates.

limitations: Three named background constructs added without new independent causal claims. Stable IDs and eleven categories preserved; no forced citation quota, numbered rows, invented yearly mentions, automatic ethical/harm edges or full-paper Markdown copy.
